..
Issued at 1124 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

An unseasonably warm 500mb high (500mb temperatures were 
greater than the 95th percentile) was centered over southeast 
Colorado and the Panhandle of Texas earlier this morning. 
Isolated evening thunderstorms that occurred near a surface 
boundary over eastern Colorado and northwest Kansas as a weak 
upper wave crosses that area have dissipated as of 10pm CDT. A 
similar setup is expected across western Kansas on Monday with 
evening thunderstorms once again being possible near the surface
boundary that by late Monday as another subtle wave is forecast
to cross northwest Kansas. Only difference is that this surface
boundary will be located a little further east. As a result 
there will be a slight chance for a few thunderstorms west and 
north of the Garden City area late day. What storms that do 
develop late day will move east towards north central Kansas 
early Monday night and weaken. Currently severe weather is not 
anticipated, however isolated gusty winds will be possible from 
a few of the stronger storms north and west of the Garden City 
area. 

Dangerous heat will continue on Monday. Little change in air 
mass is expected across southwest Kansas for the start of the 
work week. 850Mb temperatures will once again be in the 33 to 35
degree range with the models showing less than a 3C spread in 
these temperatures between the 25th and 75th percentile. Not 
only this but also the late latest Extreme forecast index is 
between 0.8 to 0.9 with a shift of tails greater than zero. All 
this suggests a high confidence forecast for temperatures to 
once again climb back into the 105 to near 110 degree range. 
Based on this the ongoing heat advisory that is currently out 
for all of southwest Kansas still looks on track. Do however 
have a concern about portions of south central Kansas and a few 
areas along the I-70 corridor. From roughly Hays to Medicine 
Lodge where the overnight lows will again for the second night 
stay near 80 degrees. These overnight lows will not provide much
relief to the heat of the past few days. Also based on how 
temperatures/heat index values performed today compared to the 
NBM forecast along with good collaboration with our neighbor 
will go ahead and upgrade the Heat Advisory to a Extreme Heat 
Warning for areas along an east of a Hays to Larned to Medicine 
Lodge line on Monday despite that many locations may end up 
being a degree or two shy of the 110 afternoon heat index. Will 
continue to monitor this closely and if needed expand it 
westward if required.

The upper high will begin to shift south/southwest on Tuesday 
which will allow for stronger westerly flow to develop across 
the Central Rockies which will be near the north/northeastern 
edge of the upper high by Tuesday night. As the same time a 
surface cold front will drop into southwest Kansas by Wednesday.
This will result in a brief break in the summer heat for some 
locations along with increasing thunderstorm chances. Currently 
based on the latest models it appears that the best chances for 
rain towards mid week will be across west central and north 
central Kansas. The chances will then expand across much of 
southwest Kansas late week as a northwesterly flow develops as 
the upper high/ridge builds across the western United States.

As mentioned earlier the temperatures will briefly cool some, 
but not much, towards mid week as the cold front moves into 
southwest Kansas. However highs around 100 will still be 
possible during the afternoon on Tuesday prior to the frontal 
passage given the warm downslope westerly flow ahead of the cold
front. Timing of this surface boundary that far out is still 
somewhat unclear but latest ensemble continue to support that 
areas near the Oklahoma border, especially south central Kansas 
will stay south of the cold front through Wednesday. This will 
result in ongoing highs around 100 with heat index values of 
around 105 possible. Later shifts will need to monitor this 
closely for possibly needing to extending the heat advisory for 
some areas given the ongoing dangerous heat. Despite the cold 
fronts arrival mid week, the temperatures will stay unseasonably
warm in the upper 90s to around 100 for most locations through 
the end of the work week.
